input.text: Root source review while implementation is active: aws_observation.observe currently proves the original stack/token completed, then constructs Collector from config.instance_id; Collector.instance checks that configured ID/account but there is no native stack-resource membership binding. A healthy unrelated EC2 in the same account/VPC could satisfy that target. Also an immutable pre-deploy config cannot know a newly allocated EC2 instance ID for CREATE. Resolve the instance from an explicit compiled logical-resource selector via the original stack/native resource readback (with exact resource type/stack binding), then bind all observations to that actual ID; do not accept an arbitrary configured ID as deployment provenance. Equivalent Azure linkage must bind its VM to the original deployment/template/operation rather than a healthy arbitrary ID. This is an early static call-path finding, not a claimed executed exploit or independent verdict. Preserve CREATE as a usable native path; owner setup cannot predeclare a random future EC2 ID. Add actual substituted-resource tests and supported CREATE resolution tests before the fix.
